### iliad-108 (17.1–105)

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| ἀγάσσατο (17.71, εἰ μή οἱ ἀγάσσατο Φοῖβος Ἀπόλλων) | "had not begrudged it to him" | "had not begrudged him this" | "grudged", "been jealous of", "resented" (νεμεσσάω "feel resentment" is kept for νεμεσσάω, 17.93, 17.100); ἀγάομαι "begrudge" |
| ἰύζουσιν (17.66, κύνες τ’ ἄνδρές τε νομῆες … πολλὰ μάλ’ ἰύζουσιν) | "very loudly raise a cry" | "raise a great cry" | "shout" (kept for ἄϋσε), "cry out" (kept for ἰάχων), "shriek" (κεκλήγων), "yell" (turned down at 5.591); ἰύζω "raise a cry" |
| ὀρεσίτροφος (λέων, 17.61) | "mountain-nurtured" | "mountain-nurtured" | "mountain-bred", "reared on the mountains"; follows the table’s διοτρεφής "Zeus-nurtured" and ἐλεόθρεπτος "marsh-nurtured" (-τροφος "nurtured") |
| ὀλοόφρων (κάπρου, 17.21) | "baneful-minded" | "baneful-minded" | "destructive", "deadly-minded"; follows ὀλοός "baneful" (3.133, 16.701) |
| ἀσβέστῳ (φλογὶ … Ἡφαίστοιο, 17.89) | "unquenchable" | "unquenchable" | "unslakeable", "unfading"; σβέννυμι "quench" (16.621) |
| ἀκίχητα (ἵππους, 17.75) | "unreachable" | "which cannot be overtaken" | "uncatchable", "out of reach"; the form is the negative of κιχάνω "reach" |
| ἀρητὸν … γόον (17.37; meaning not certain) | "cursed lament" | "cursed lament" (+ note: from ἀρά "prayer, curse"; "accursed" is the usual guess) | "prayed-for", "much-prayed-for", "longed-for" |
| ἀπείρητος · ἀδήριτος (πόνος, 17.41–42) | "untried" · "undecided" | "untried" · "undecided" | "unproven", "unfought", "uncontested"; ἀδήριτος from δῆρις "contest" |
| ἐκ θεόφιν (17.101) | "from gods" | "with divine help" (+ note: -φιν marks no number) | "from the gods", "from a god" (each decides the number), "by the gods’ will" |
| γνωτόν (17.35, ἐμὸν τὸν ἔπεφνες) | "kinsman" | "kinsman" | "brother"; follows the table’s γνωτόν "a kinsman" (13.696); the Greek does not say which relation |
| ἀναχωρήσαντα (17.30) · ἀναχαζομένοιο (17.47) | "stepping back" · "as he gave ground" | "step back" · "gave ground backward" | "retreating", "withdrawing"; follows the table’s ἀναχωρήσας "stepping back" (5.107) and χάζομαι "give ground" |
| πληθύν (ἐς πληθὺν ἰέναι, 17.31) | "the crowd" | "the crowd" | "throng" (kept for ὅμιλος), "multitude" |
| περιβάς (Πατρόκλῳ, 17.80) | "having bestridden" | "standing over" | "straddling", "covering"; περιβαίνω "bestride" (cf. βαῖνε, 17.4, 17.6) |
| ὅς κεν ἴδηται (17.93, 17.100) | "whoever sees it" · "whoever sees me" | "whoever sees it" · "who sees me give way" | "whoever sees" alone (the object differs: the armour at 93, Menelaus himself at 100) |
| ὤ μοι ἐγών (17.91) | "Oh me" | "Oh me" | "Alas", "Woe is me"; follows the table’s ὤ μοι ἐγών (16.433) |
| ἄγχι δ’ ἄρ’ αὐτοῦ ἔστη (17.10–11) | "near him he took his stand" | "took his stand close by him" | "stood by him"; ἵστημι aorist intransitive "take one’s stand" |
| ὣς εἰπὼν οὔτησε κατ’ ἀσπίδα πάντοσ’ ἐΐσην (17.43) | same `l` as the published iliad-068 | "With these words Euphorbus stabbed at the shield of Menelaus, which was equal on every side" | the published `i` has "stabbed at him on his shield"; the subject and owner are named, because in this part the speaker has just changed (Menelaus to Euphorbus) and "him" would point back wrongly |
| ἀκωκή (17.49, ἁπαλοῖο δι’ αὐχένος ἤλυθ’ ἀκωκή) | "the point" | "the point" | "tip" (the table’s δουρὸς ἀκωκή, 11.253, 16.323, is the tip of a spear in the hand; here the Odyssey’s published line, with "point", is kept) |
| ὃ δὲ δεύτερος ὄρνυτο χαλκῷ … ἐπευξάμενος Διὶ πατρί (17.45–46) | "and he in second place rushed on with the bronze" … "having prayed to father Zeus;" | "rushed on second with the bronze, after praying to father Zeus;" | the published iliad-019 wording, but the closing ":" is replaced by ";" (no speech follows here) |
| καί μιν φωνήσας ἔπεα πτερόεντα προσηύδα (17.74) | "and, lifting his voice, to him winged words he spoke:" | "and lifting his voice he spoke winged words to him:" | the published pronoun "her" (1.201); the table’s 2.7 row also changes the pronoun. The line stands inside a three-line unit, so the validator’s whole-unit rule does not apply |
| ὑπέρβιον (εὐχετάασθαι, 17.19) | "exceedingly" | "exceedingly" | "to excess" (the first draft), "overbearingly" (kept for ὑπερηνορέοντες), "beyond measure"; follows the Odyssey table’s ὑπέρβιος "exceeding" and ὑπέρβιον "with exceeding violence"; εὐχετάομαι is "boast" here (the sense of a taunt), not the "pray" of the table’s 6.268 row |
